description: Problem: the installed rule ~/.omp/agent/rules/code-first.md makes the agent read the code skill at its first edit or write of a source file. It was tested only together with a rewritten skill description, while the installed setup uses the current description, so the installed combination is untested. The scenario file of the first test was not kept, so nothing can be repeated. Outcome: a committed, repeatable scenario set and a measurement of the rule with the current description. Arms on Sonnet 5.5, 3 sessions per prompt: current description with no rule; current description with the rule. Decision gate, fixed before the runs: report sessions where the rule fired and, among those, sessions that read the skill. If the skill is read in fewer than 95% of firing sessions, or the rule fires in any near-miss session, report to the owner and do not change the installed rule. Otherwise record that the installed setup behaves as the first test did. Guardrails: (1) agents under test run only in /tmp/omp-ablation sandboxes through evals/ablation/run.py, replay.py or the loading-map probe; (2) change nothing under ~/.omp/agent, ~/.claude or ~/.agents while sessions run, upgrade neither omp, Claude Code nor tractable-mcp during a run, and start no run while another evaluation is running; (3) commit the pre-registration (hypothesis, arms, checks, sample, decision, Holm family and alpha) before any scored session; smoke runs never count; (4) use a new out folder and a ledger with the ceiling stated here; stop at the ceiling and report; raising it needs the owner's approval in a later message; (5) record the omp, Claude Code and tractable-mcp versions with the results; never pool new sessions with results from another harness version; new comparisons form their own Holm family and published bands are left unchanged; (6) existing scenarios and pre-registration files are not edited: new arms use new scenario ids and a new pre-registration file, and run.py report or phase3_bands.py over the existing result folders gives the same output before and after; (7) read at least 5 transcripts per arm before reporting any number, and report grader faults found; (8) delete or weaken no instruction or skill text on this evidence; (9) a published number in a report is never rewritten: add a dated note after it; (10) scenario and scratch code that produced a result is committed with it; (11) if a result changes a claim in the blog post 'Testing agent instructions', correct the draft by PR, or if the post is published add a dated correction note and update its 'updated' time; (12) publish by task branch and draft PR with identity Joe Harris <joeharris76@gmail.com>; the item stays open until its PR is merged through the repository's usual flow (green CI, squash merge), and anything this item reserves for the owner is not merged or installed without the owner's message. Spend ceiling 25 USD. Extra: run.py disables every user rule by file name, so the sandbox rule file must have a name not used in ~/.omp/agent/rules (for example code-first-under-test.md), and one smoke session must show it firing before any counted run; the rule under test lives in the sandbox repository's .omp/rules, never in the user's rules directory; check one overlay to confirm user rules are still disabled.
